source_message.text:
3.3V rail (AXP2101 DCDC1, 2A) — this is the main power source whenever the power board is attached:
\- ESP32-S3 module
\- INA219
\- Every I2C sensor (SCD41, BME280, ENS160) through the sensor board
\- I2C display
\- TTP223, AM312 PIR

5V rail (MT3608 boost, 500mA) — ESP32 GPIO3 controls this rail:
\- SPS30 particulate sensor
\- ZE08-CH2O formaldehyde sensor
\- SK6812 LEDs (when connected to 5V — version-dependent)

3.3V rail (ME6211A LDO, 1A) — active only if the main board's USB-C is connected WITHOUT the power board:
\- It supplies the same 3.3V rail listed above. With Schottky diode OR-ing, whichever source is available takes precedence. This is for standalone programming.

Battery (3.7–4.2V) — supplies the AXP2101, which subsequently powers everything listed above.

The simple rule is that the AXP2101 supplies everything during normal operation. The LDO activates only for programming when the power board is not connected.

value_updates.led_load_power: SK6812 LEDs when configured for 5V operation

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Apologies, GPIO3 came from my original ESP32 design, so that was my mistake. You can assign 5V_EN to GPIO5. I also noticed that the WROOM-1 module does not expose GPIO22, 23, 25, or 27, so I need to remap SCL0 (GPIO22→38) and SPI MOSI (GPIO23→26). I will revise the documentation and send you the complete updated GPIO table.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: The LEDs now use 3.3V power rather than 5V. With a 3.3V supply, the SK6812 data threshold decreases to 2.31V, and the ESP32 3.3V output meets it directly, eliminating the need for a level shifter. The downside is that 3.3V is somewhat below the SK6812 datasheet minimum of 3.7V, although it operates reliably at indicator brightness levels.
